subject: Clarify commercial model for RFP: volume acceleration & reconciliation
messages:
From: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@orchardhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T14:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify commercial model for RFP: volume acceleration & reconciliation

Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP appendix. Procurement and Finance had a few clarifying questions specifically about the commercial/pricing section. Can you confirm the behavior for the following items so we can include the answers in our vendor evaluation? We need this by EOW if possible.

Key questions:
- Baseline token price: please provide unit price per 1k generation tokens and per 1k embedding tokens for the model families you listed (small, standard, large). Indicate whether these are list or committed prices.
- Volume acceleration discounts: how do you apply discounts when usage accelerates mid-term? Is there an up-front accelerator credit, or is it applied at invoice true-up?
- Overage treatment: if we exceed committed volume in a billing period, what multiplier or tiered rates apply? Are there gracebands for initial ramp?
- Prepayment treatment and clawbacks: if we prepay and later terminate or don't consume, what reconciliation / prorata / clawback applies?
- Reconciliation cadence: monthly/quarterly true-up? Cash offset or invoiced charge?
- Impact on Dedicated/Private pricing: is Dedicated billed differently or carved out?
- SLA credit treatment vs commercial credits: if outages occur, any offset to committed volumes or dollar credits?

Attached: RFP_Appendix_C.pdf (our current commercial template).

If it helps, we can do a 30-min call on Friday to go through specifics.

Best,
Sarah
Procurement Manager — Orchard Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-15T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify commercial model for RFP: volume acceleration & reconciliation

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise commercial summary tailored to the questions in Appendix C. I've attached a short PDF (Commercial_Summary_v1.pdf) that mirrors this language for inclusion in your RFP appendix. High-level points first, then line items.

High level
- List pricing is published; we provide committed (discounted) pricing when customers agree to a monthly or annual consumption commitment. Discounts increase with committed tier and with annual prepayment.
- Volume acceleration: discounts earned by accelerated consumption are applied at the reconciliation/true-up. We provide an "acceleration credit" that reduces the next invoice (or is paid out as a credit balance) once the higher tier is reached and validated at true-up.
- Overage: default overage rate = 1.50x of the committed per-token rate for that tier; we can opt for a tiered overage ladder for large commitments. A 10% graceband can be applied in the initial 90-day ramp period by mutual agreement.
- Prepayment/clawback: prepaid amounts are reconciled at the quarterly true-up; unconsumed prepaid balances are prorated and returned less an administrative reconciliation fee (standard 3%) unless an annual prepay discount was provided — then a 2% early termination adjustment applies to protect the prepay concession.
- Reconciliation cadence: quarterly true-up by default (monthly available on request for Enterprise billing). True-up is netted on the subsequent invoice; surplus credits are kept as account credit or refunded by wire if requested.
- Dedicated/Private: Dedicated pricing is quoted separately (capacity-based) and not included in token-commit tiers; however, customers can hybridize (committed hosted tokens + Dedicated pools) — we provide cross-product accounting in the true-up.
- SLA credits: SLA dollar credits are separate from consumption credits and do not offset consumption true-ups. SLA credits are issued as a percentage of monthly service fees per the SLA schedule.

Line items (examples)
- Baseline (list) generation model family: Small $2.00 / 1k tokens; Standard $6.00 / 1k tokens; Large $18.00 / 1k tokens.
- Baseline (list) embedding model: Emb-Standard $1.25 / 1k tokens.
- Committed tier example (annual prepay): 25M tokens/month -> 15% discount off list for Standard family; 50M/month -> 25% discount; 100M+/month -> 33% discount.
- Acceleration credit: when rolling 30-day usage exceeds committed tier, we calculate the incremental discount differential and apply as a credit at the next quarterly true-up.
- Overage: 1.5x committed per-token rate by default; negotiated tiered overage rates available for >100% sustained overage.
- Billing: quarterly true-up; invoice netting (account credit applied against next invoice).

Open items where we ask for clarification from your side
1) Would Orchard prefer monthly true-ups instead of quarterly for cash-heavy reconciliation?
2) Is there appetite for an initial 90-day ramp graceband (we can include a one-time 10% cushion)?
3) Do you require prepayment escrow or locked funds?

If this matches what you need I can loop in Karthik and Marissa to finalize concession language and produce an updated PDF for inclusion in Appendix C. Happy to hop on Friday — suggest 11am PT.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Commercial_Summary_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify commercial model for RFP: volume acceleration & reconciliation

Team —

Quick internal notes on the draft we send to Orchard. Keeping it tight for legal/sales:
- Overage multiplier: 1.5x is our standard, but for mid-market buyers we typically drop to 1.25x for the first two billing periods after a ramp if we include a 10% graceband. I recommend we offer 1.25x (Q1 & Q2) with reversion to 1.5x thereafter unless they re-contract.
- Graceband: strong +1 for a one-time 10% cushion for the first 90 days; reduces churn risk and looks good in procurement scoring. Mark it as "startup ramp protection" in the appendix.
- Prepay discounts: offering 2% additional discount for full annual prepay is industry standard; however, we need clear clawback formula: prorated refund less admin + protection for the prepay discount we gave (we should factor 60 days notice or liquidated damages on early termination to avoid gaming).
- Dedicated carve-out: ensure we call out that Dedicated is priced as reserved capacity and not token-based; provide an optional appendix with hybrid accounting methodology.

Action items:
- Irene: update Commercial_Summary_v2 to reflect 1.25x overage for first two quarters and 10% 90-day graceband. Add prepay clawback formula language (simple math example).
- Marissa: prepare negotiation bullets for AE and CS to use in playbook (we'll want one-liners for procurement).

Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tang <sarah.tang@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify commercial model for RFP: volume acceleration & reconciliation

Sarah —

Thanks again. Per our internal review we've made a couple of pragmatic adjustments that should be procurement-friendly while protecting our economics. Summary of the adjusted commercial terms (we're happy to include this redline in Appendix C):

Finalized items
- Graceband: one-time 10% cushion applied to the committed tier for the first 90 days following go-live ("ramp protection").
- Overage: 1.25x of committed per-token rate for the first two billing quarters following the ramp; reverts to 1.50x thereafter. For customers with >100M tokens/month sustained overage we can propose a tiered ladder instead of the multiplier.
- Acceleration credit: acceleration discounts are validated at the quarterly true-up and applied as an account credit (can net against the next invoice). We will include a worked example in the PDF.
- Prepayment/clawback: annual prepay qualifies for an extra 2% discount. If the customer terminates early or consumes less than prepaid, the unconsumed prepaid balance is returned (wire) or applied as credit less a prorated clawback equal to the prepay discount benefit and a 2% reconciliation fee (example included).
- Reconciliation cadence: quarterly by default; we can support monthly true-up for enterprise billing ops.
- Dedicated/Private: Dedicated remains capacity-priced and is excluded from token commit tiers; hybrid accounting is available and will be included as an optional appendix.
- SLA credits: remain separate and do not offset consumption reconciliation.

Attachments: I've attached Commercial_Summary_v2.pdf with redlined language and a short worked example of the acceleration-credit math. Also included a link for signature when you're ready: docusign_orchard_2027_link.txt

Next steps
1) If this looks right, please confirm acceptance of these clauses and we will provide a final Appendix C.
2) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call Friday 11am PT to walk the finance and procurement teams through the worked example.

Appreciate the collaboration — we've designed these terms to be audit-friendly and easy to reconcile for billing ops.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
